subject: future
topic: Automation is creating a 'hollowed out' middle class of cognitive skills
angle: While automation and offshoring are linked to middle-skill job losses in high-income countries, the observed polarization of the labor market is significantly influenced by low-skilled immigration and varies by country development.
title: The Hollowed Out Middle

hooks.text: Is automation actually destroying the middle class?
You think it is robots. The data suggests it is migration.
You are watching the middle of the labor market vanish.
An empty desk in a gray office.

reveal.headline: Labor polarization disappears when only native workers are considered.
reveal.body: The shift toward high- and low-skill jobs is significantly influenced by low-skilled immigration rather than just technological change.

explain.headline: The evidence on automation is mixed.
explain.body: While some countries show an expansion of high- and low-paid jobs, other studies show no evidence of task-biased technological change or labor polarization in developing nations.

matters.headline: The middle class is being hollowed out.
matters.body: That may be why you see fewer middle-skill job opportunities today. The erosion of these roles contributes to lower male participation rates in the workforce.

verdict: The evidence shows that while routine tasks are being automated and middle-skill jobs are declining in some contexts, the broader labor market polarization is complex and influenced by migration and regional differences.
caveat: The evidence for task-biased technological change is not conclusive and varies significantly depending on the time period and the specific population (e.g., native vs. immigrant workers) being studied.
caption:
The middle class of cognitive skills is being hollowed out. 

Research shows that labor polarization is complex. While middle-skill jobs are declining in some areas, the trend is heavily influenced by immigration and varies by country development. The evidence for task-biased technological change remains inconclusive and varies by population.
